newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end lower, feeders off sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end lower, feeders off sharply.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower but above the day's lows, with prices hit by fund-sparked technical long liquidation, traders said.

Live cattle ended 0.775 to 0.250 cent a lb lower with December down 0.750 at 66.525 cents. Feeder cattle tumbled for limit losses of 1.500 cents in January and March earlier but recovered slightly to finish 1.225 to to 0.700 cent lower with January off most at 65.775 cents. November expired earlier at 64.400 cents, down 0.125 cent on the day.
Technical selling developed in live cattle futures when they broke through a trend line Wednesday.

Futures looked technically weak after setting a new contract high last Friday and then trending lower. A break in the trend line and a rise in open interest Wednesday on a lower close prompted funds to liquidate, sending prices down to nearly 4-week lows. Sell stops were touched off under 67.000 cents a lb and again under 66.900 cents, traders said.

Lower fed cattle prices Wednesday and evening of positions ahead of Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report also weighed on the market. However, commercial support developed to pare losses after midday.
Feedlots sold cattle just to stay current, analysts said.
"Fundamentally, you're still in good shape on this (cattle) market, probably a lot better than most of us thought we would be at this time," John Nalivka, President of Sterling Marketing Inc.
"The feedlots are current and you have a record spread on the choice to select and there are not many choice cattle around," he said.

Nalivka added that with feedlots moving their cattle at a profit and remaining current, there is a good chance that there will be additional strength in cash cattle markets the week after Thanksgiving.
Fund liquidation weighed heavily on feeders and sell stops took prices limit down early before bouncing slightly late on short covering. "Funds were very heavily long the market," one trader said.

Higher corn futures, the initial break in live cattle and concern over growing fed cattle numbers added to overall weakness. Sell stops were touched off under 66.650 cents, basis January, and again under 66.000 cents, traders said.
Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report is expected to show feedlot supplies rising to year-ago levels and this led to ideas that feedlots are full, one trader added.

Estimates for November 1 on-feed supplies in large feedlots in the seven key states averaged 99.5 percent of a year ago with October placements averaging 105.7 percent and marketings averaging 97.3 percent of last year.

In live cattle options, there was late buying of December 66 and 67 puts, thought to be short covering. Earlier traders bought February 64 calls and sold June 64 calls which boosted February volitility to 16.5 percent, pit sources said.
Cargill Investor Services spread long May feeders/short October live cattle and long March feeders/short August live cattle, pit sources added.
